newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine aims to raise $1 bln from Sept bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine aims to raise $1 bln from Sept bond issues.

text.p: Ukraine wants to raise $1 billion from Samurai and Eurobonds it plans to launch in September, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of reforms Serhiy Tyhypko told a news conference on Thursday.
"We plan to get $1 billion through the issues," Tyhypko said.
Ukraine has previously announced plans to launch yen-denominated bonds on the Japanese market in September, followed in the same month by a Eurobond denominated in dollars or German marks.

Ukrainian officials said previously the former Soviet republic planned to raise $350-500 million from Eurobonds. Central bank governor Viktor Yushchenko said in April Ukraine wanted to raise $300-900 million from Samurai and Eurobonds this year to partially finance the 1997 budget deficit.
Ukraine has yet to receive a rating for its first foreign bond launches, and Tyhpyko said work on a rating would begin in earnest next week.
He said he did not expect delays in a long-term International Monetary Fund loan would influence the country's rating.
"What will affect our rating is when we start real economic changes. The world is waiting for our bonds," he said, adding Ukraine had to work on eliminating corruption and speeding up reforms.
